claim: Administrative-AI accountability gap: Directive scope + LCO (Ch 10)
detail: ✅ CONFIRMED 2026-06-19. The federal Treasury Board Directive on Automated Decision-Making (in force 2019) applies ONLY to federal institutions and public-facing systems — so provincial welfare, policing, and courts (the highest-impact administrative-AI domains) fall OUTSIDE it (the jurisdictional gap). Law Commission of Ontario, "Accountable AI" (June 2022, 19 recs): do not deploy high-risk government AI before a binding "Trustworthy AI" framework in legislation; Ontario should adopt a provincial equivalent of the federal Directive; "systemic legal issues cannot be addressed through individual litigation, 'ethical AI' guidelines, or piecemeal legislation." Admin-law backstop: *Vavilov* (2019 SCC 65) centres the right to intelligible reasons → the black-box challenge; Charter s.7/s.15 angles are anticipatory (no tested Canadian government-algorithm precedent).
